module.purpose: Provides React's `act` testing utility to wrap code, batch updates, and flush pending renderer tasks synchronously or asynchronously within nested scopes.
module.summary: This module implements the `act` function used in React tests to ensure deterministic flushing of state updates and effects. It tracks nested act scopes via a depth counter, queues renderer tasks on ReactSharedInternals, and supports both synchronous callbacks and thenable-returning async callbacks. Helpers flush the queue, recursively process async work via macrotasks, aggregate errors, and warn if an act call is not awaited. Legacy mode behavior is conditionally replicated based on a feature flag.
module.businessContext: Testing infrastructure for React components. Broken act leads to flaky tests and undetected async updates in test suites.

detail.name: popActScope
detail.signature: function popActScope(prevActQueue: null | Array<RendererTask>, prevActScopeDepth: number)
preconditions: The global mutable state variable actScopeDepth must exist and be accessible.
The __DEV__ flag determines whether the overlap check is performed.
postconditions: In __DEV__ mode, if prevActScopeDepth is not exactly actScopeDepth - 1, a console.error diagnostic is emitted.
The global actScopeDepth is restored to the value of prevActScopeDepth (in __DEV__ mode only).
invariants: actScopeDepth is only mutated within this function when __DEV__ is true.
edgeCases: If prevActScopeDepth does not equal actScopeDepth - 1, the overlap error message is triggered and actScopeDepth is still updated.
In production builds (__DEV__ is false), no validation or depth restoration occurs.

errorPolicy.onInvalidInput: No invalid input path; behavior depends only on the relationship between prevActScopeDepth and the global actScopeDepth.

stateMutations: Mutates the module-level global variable actScopeDepth, assigning it the value of prevActScopeDepth (only when __DEV__ is true).
detail.summary: Restores the previous act scope depth during act teardown, surfacing a dev-mode diagnostic when overlapping act() calls are detected.

units.name: recursivelyFlushAsyncActWork

detail.name: recursivelyFlushAsyncActWork
detail.signature: function recursivelyFlushAsyncActWork<T>(returnValue: T, resolve: T => mixed, reject: mixed => mixed)
preconditions: Must only execute when __DEV__ is truthy (compiled out in production builds).
ReactSharedInternals.actQueue, if non-null, must be either null or an array.
resolve and reject must be valid function values.
postconditions: On successful completion with no thrown errors, resolve is called with returnValue.
If any errors were thrown during flushing, all collected errors are aggregated via aggregateErrors and passed to reject.
ReactSharedInternals.thrownErrors is cleared to empty length before calling reject.
invariants: While asynchronously scheduled tasks remain in the act queue, the queue is repeatedly flushed until empty.
Once the queue is empty, ReactSharedInternals.actQueue is set to null to signal that flushing is complete.
edgeCases: actQueue is null: skips flushing loop and proceeds directly to error check and resolve/reject.
actQueue is non-null but empty: sets actQueue to null then proceeds to resolve/reject.
flushActQueue throws during execution: caught and pushed into ReactSharedInternals.thrownErrors, leaving remaining queue items intact.
Multiple rounds of async scheduling: each round is handled by re-invoking recursivelyFlushAsyncActWork via queueMacrotask.
stateMutations: ReactSharedInternals.thrownErrors (pushed to on error, cleared before reject)
detail.summary: Recursively flushes the React act queue of async work by draining queued microtasks/macrotasks until no scheduled tasks remain, resolving the promise on completion or rejecting it if any errors were aggregated during flushing.
